title: Runtime descriptor
description: How the session attaches to one runtime and turns its records into runtime events. A descriptor matches and copies; it never computes. runtimes/<name>/descriptor.yaml, with fixtures beside it.

version.description: The descriptor format. Forager refuses a version it does not read.

runtime.description: The runtime this describes, as the launch spec sets it: claude, codex.

title.description: The runtime's display name: Claude Code. runtimes.json lists it beside the name.

runtime_version.description: The version of the runtime the descriptor expects, the one qory image check compares with an image's program. Reported in dev.qory.session.started; Forager never checks the installed version.

sources.description: How the session attaches. The terminal bytes are always captured and need no source: there is nothing in them to match.

output.description: Structured output on the runtime's standard output, when the session runs on pipes.

format.description: jsonl: one JSON object per line. Lines that are not JSON objects are not records.

hooks.description: Hook calls the runtime makes. The session installs its forwarder as a command hook for each listed event in the settings the launch passes; the forwarder writes what it reads on its standard input to the local socket as one record.

install.description: How the session installs its forwarder, chosen among the ways the binary implements. claude-settings: a command hook per event, added to the JSON settings file the launch passes with --settings, or to a new one when it passes none.

events.description: The runtime's hook event names to install the forwarder for, in the runtime's spelling.

stop.description: How the session stops the runtime, at a run's time limit or when Forager itself is stopped. Runtimes differ in what a signal means, one closes its session on SIGINT and drops it on SIGTERM, and this sets which the runtime gets. A run that sets a signal or a grace overrides it; absent, SIGTERM and ten seconds.

signal.description: The signal that requests the runtime's exit, among the ones the session sends.

grace.description: How long the runtime has after the signal before SIGKILL, as a duration: 30s.

headless.description: The arguments that mean the runtime runs without an interface. When one of them is among the arguments the runtime is started with, the session runs on pipes even at a terminal, exactly as when the caller requests pipes: the runtime is recorded as not interactive and the output source is read. Absent, the caller alone decides.

args.description: The arguments, each as the runtime spells it. A short one matches the whole token (-p); a long one matches the token or its --name=value form (--print, --print=...). Nothing else is inferred: a runtime that takes its prompt on standard input has no argument to list, and its caller sets headless itself.

secrets.description: The secrets the runtime needs and the variables it keeps for itself. runtimes.json lists the secrets of every descriptor the contract ships.

declares.description: The secrets the runtime reads, each from one variable, and where its value is set.

id.description: The declaration's id, unique among the declarations.

title.description: What the secret is, for a person choosing one.

name.description: The variable the runtime reads the secret from.

hosts.description: The hosts the value is set on: exact DNS names, no wildcard, no IP literal.

paths.description: The paths of those hosts the value is set on, in the policy's path grammar. Absent means every path.

auth.description: How the value is set on a request, a scheme from the closed set, without account_header and account_claim, which only an API credential of a run configuration has. A variable that is also a key's in model.keys has the same auth there.

one_of.description: Groups of declarations of which the runtime needs at most one, and exactly one of a required group. of lists declared ids, each id in at most one group; a declaration in no group is optional.

reserves.description: Variables the runtime reads a credential from beside the declared ones. Behind a wall, a declared or reserved variable that nothing sets, neither a placeholder, the run, the runtime's preparation, Forager nor the wall, is unset inside.

denies.description: Variables the session always leaves out of the server's set for the runtime, and reports: the ones that move where the runtime sends its requests and credentials, or change what it runs.

credential_files.description: Files in which the runtime keeps its credential, ~ being the home of the user Forager runs as.

model.description: The model API formats the runtime sends its requests in, where a composer writes a run's model id, effort value and model endpoint for the runtime, and the variables it reads a model key from. runtimes.json lists it for every descriptor that has one.

formats.description: The model API formats the runtime sends its requests in, each from api-format.schema.json.

model.description: Where the run's model id goes.

effort.description: Where an effort value goes, and the values the runtime accepts there. Absent, the runtime has no place for one.

run.description: Where the run's effort value goes.

agent.description: Where an agent's effort value goes, in the agent's file. Absent, the runtime has no place for an agent's effort.

endpoint.description: Where the base URL of the run's model API goes, exactly one of: variable, the variable the runtime reads it from; setting, a dotted key of the runtime's settings, which the session writes as a place's setting, the URL as a TOML string with config. A flag is no place of the endpoint.

variable.description: The variable the runtime reads the base URL from.

setting.description: The dotted key of the runtime's settings the base URL goes in, such as model_providers.qory.base_url.

keys.description: The variables the runtime reads a model key from, one per API format and auth: the session gives an API credential's placeholder to the variable of the key whose format is the credential's and whose auth has the credential's scheme, the same header name, case ignored, and the same oauth. Each format is one of formats, each pair of format and auth appears once, and a variable is none of denies, overrides and the endpoint's variable.

format.description: The API format the key is for.

auth.description: How the runtime sends the key, without account_header and account_claim, which only an API credential of a run configuration has.

variable.description: The variable the runtime reads the key from.

overrides.description: The variables that would override the model id or effort value a composer writes. Behind a wall the session leaves each one's value out, of the server's, the run's, the machine's and the harness's values, the harness's computed values included, records it as denied, and unsets the name inside when nothing else sets it. Without a wall they change nothing.

tools.description: What the session copies from a tool's input onto the runtime's tool events.

summary.description: A tool's name, as the runtime reports it in tool, mapped to one dotted path inside the tool's input. On dev.qory.runtime.tool_started, tool_finished and tool_failed of a listed tool, the session sets summary to the member of input at that path when it is a string, copied and not computed. The 1 KiB limit applies to each summary value, not to the tools.summary table: the session cuts each summary at 1 KiB (1024 bytes) of UTF-8, at a character boundary.

fixed.description: The variables the session sets for the runtime in every launch, walled or not, by name: no value of the server, the run, the machine, the harness or the environment the run inherits applies to one. dev.qory.run.policy_applied lists the values that lost, and why, by the rules in the contract's README, Variables, The record of the variables. In a launch with a forwarder, the session sets each in a file it copies whose values reach the runtime's environment, in place of the file's value. A name is no name denied-variables.json lists, and none of the descriptor's other variables: a declared or reserved secret's, a denied one, a model key's, the model endpoint's or an override.

config.description: How the session passes settings to a runtime that reads them as TOML, such as Codex: flag, the argument that takes one key=value pair, such as --config, where key is a dotted key and value a TOML value; and fixed, the settings the session passes in every launch, walled or not. With config, a place's setting goes to flag too, its value as a TOML string. Absent, a setting goes in the JSON settings file the launch passes.

flag.description: The argument that takes one key=value pair, such as --config. The session passes one pair per argument.

fixed.description: The settings the session passes in every launch, by dotted key: 1 to 64 keys, each a TOML value, a string, a boolean or an integer, which the session writes in TOML's form, such as {model_provider: qory, features.plugins: false}. A key is none of the model section's settings, and no key is a dotted prefix of another.

egress_hosts.description: The hosts the runtime needs to reach: exact DNS names, no wildcard, no IP literal. runtimes.json lists them for every descriptor the contract ships, for a server to allow for a run; a machine's policy can still block them. This list differs from secrets.declares[].hosts, the hosts a secret's value is set on.

resume.description: Where the runtime writes the transcript of its session, and how the session starts the runtime again from it. The session reads the transcript as the runtime appends to it and writes it as dev.qory.session.transcript. In a run with resume in its run configuration, it writes the paused run's transcript at the run configuration's resume.path before the runtime starts, and adds args after the argument after, or at the end. Absent, the runtime has no resume: the session writes no dev.qory.session.transcript, and a continuation starts the runtime without a resume.

path_from.description: The member of a hook's input that contains the transcript's path, such as transcript_path. The session takes the path from the first hook input that contains it. Absent, the session takes the path from path alone.

path.description: The transcript's path when no hook input contains path_from: a template, with {session_id} replaced by the runtime's session id from dev.qory.runtime.started, and {cwd_slug} by the runtime's working directory with every character other than an ASCII letter or digit replaced by -, such as ~/.claude/projects/{cwd_slug}/{session_id}.jsonl. A * matches any characters other than / inside one path name, for a runtime that puts a date in the path, such as ~/.codex/sessions/*/*/*/rollout-*-{session_id}.jsonl. It starts with prefix.

prefix.description: The directory the transcript must lie under, ~/ for the runtime's home, ending in /, with no *. The session reads no path outside it, no path with a .. segment, and no path through a symbolic link.

args.description: The arguments the session adds to the runtime's when it resumes, with {session_id} replaced by the run configuration's resume.session_id, such as --resume {session_id}.

after.description: The argument of the runtime's that args follow, such as exec for codex exec --json, which resumes as codex exec resume <session id> --json: the session inserts args right after the first argument equal to it. Absent, or when no argument equals it, the session adds args at the end.

parent.description: Where the runtime reports which tool call started a subagent, for parent_agent_id on dev.qory.runtime.subagent_started. A record from `source` that matches the rule contains a subagent's id and the id of the tool call that started it. The agent that made that call, in the session's dev.qory.runtime.tool_started, is the subagent's parent. Absent, the session sets no parent.

agent_id.description: The path of the subagent's id in the record.

tool_use_id.description: The path of the id of the tool call that started the subagent.

rules.description: Evaluated in order against every record of the rule's source. The first rule that matches a record produces its events: one event for a rule without each; for a rule with each, one event per element that a rule with that each matches. A record that no rule matches produces nothing.

each.description: A dotted path to an array in the record. The rule matches a record when one element of the array matches it. When it is the first rule that matches, each element, in order, produces one event: that of the first rule from this one on with the same source and each that the element matches, so one record's elements may produce events of different rules. An element that no such rule matches produces nothing. A path in match or data that starts with each. reads the element; any other path reads the record.

data.description: The event's data: each key is a field of the type's data, each value a dotted path into the record whose value is copied there unchanged. A path that does not exist leaves the field out. In a rule with each, a path that starts with each. reads the element. session, line, truncated and summary are the session's to set, and no rule sets them.

set.description: Fields of the event's data with a value of the descriptor's, for a field the record has no member for, such as {source: startup}: each key is a field of the type's data, each value a string, a number or a boolean set there as it is. A field is in one of data, set and from_started.

from_started.description: Fields of the event's data the session copies from the session's last dev.qory.runtime.started of the main agent, the one without agent_id, for a runtime whose records after the start do not contain them, such as [session_id]. Only a rule of the output source that produces another type has it. The session writes no event of the rule before such a dev.qory.runtime.started.

match.description: Every entry must match: a path into the record equals the value, a string, number or boolean; or, with {present: true}, the path exists. Nothing else: no patterns, no ranges, no expressions.

place.description: Where a value goes, exactly one of: flag, an argument the runtime is started with, which takes the value; setting, a dotted key in the JSON settings file the launch passes, or with config, a key=value pair of config.flag; variable, an environment variable.

valued_place.description: A place, and in values the values the runtime accepts there.

agent_place.description: Where a value goes in an agent's file: frontmatter, a key of the file's frontmatter, and in values the values the runtime accepts there.

toml_value.description: A TOML value of config.fixed: a string of at most 4096 characters with no NUL, carriage return or line feed, a boolean, or an integer of at most 2^53-1 either side of 0, which every JSON reader reads exactly.

key_variable.description: A variable a runtime reads a key from: a variable's name other than HOME, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS and BASH_ENV, which change what runs. The schema refuses them in upper case; Forager refuses them in any letter case.
